newsitem.title: UK: IPE fall, heavy selling, weighs on Euro fuel marke.
newsitem.headline: IPE fall, heavy selling, weighs on Euro fuel marke.

text.p: European fuel markets were under pressure on Tuesday from aggressive selling of high sulphur barges and the slump in crude futures which dragged low sulphur swaps down, traders said.
Prompt barges traded at $78 a tonne fob, with one big seller saying he had to clear his tanks to make way for Russian material. Deals were heard for delivery next month at $80 and $81 a tonne fob.
High sulphur cargoes were hardly discussed, though a Portugese utility company buy tender may bring some life to the market.
The results of the tender to purchase two 25,000 tonne cargoes, with an option for a third, all for June delivery, should be announced on Wednesday, traders said.
A distressed Russian cargo of cracked fuel was being offered into the British utility market and was believed to have eventually traded for $80 cif to an unknown buyer.

However the overhang of cracked Russian material was not so visible in the ARA area as during last week, though the EdP tender, which demands fuel have European Union origin, will do nothing to soak up the Baltic flow.
No physical one percent cargo trades were reported.
